fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. The king settled them in the towns of Samaria, and they took possession and lived there. Five different places of origin, one region. I think that's a lot of new neighbors to get used to.

The Medes are close, friend, but that's a different move. The cities of the Medes are where some of the Israelites ended up when they were carried off (2 Kings 17:6). The new people were settled in Samaria to replace them. Two groups, opposite directions.

That's a reasonable guess, but it's not what they say. Their words to the king are that the peoples don't know the requirements of the God of the land, and the lions are killing them off. Nothing about the land sitting empty. It's a heavy part of the story, friend, and the settlers name the real reason they gave.

The king doesn't pick one of his own officials. He commands them to send back one of the priests they carried off from Samaria. That's the person who is supposed to go live there and teach. The teacher comes from the priests, baker, not from the king's staff.

Gods, baker. The people of each nation kept making their own gods in the cities where they settled, even with a priest teaching them. That's not a small side project. It's a heavy thing, and the text says it plainly.

Towns aren't what they kept making, baker. The settlers lived in the towns of Samaria, and the verse says they made their own gods in the cities where they had settled. The answer is gods. Close pick, friend.
Levites and Jerusalem don't show up in this verse, baker. The text says they appointed for themselves priests of all sorts. They did the choosing. Careful with that word "only."

Customs is it. They worshiped the LORD, but they also served their own gods according to the customs of the nations from which they had been carried away. They kept the old habits from back home. I've kept habits too long myself, friend, and mine were just about cookie sizes.
